answer: A mechanism that actually bites: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because meadow only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, voyage is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
